summary.title: Facebook Threat Model
summary.description: Threat model for Facebook social media application covering authentication, data storage, messaging, and content features. Based on STRIDE analysis, Attack Tree, and Attack Library findings.

threats.title: Fake Facebook Login Page (Phishing)
threats.description: Threat actor creates a fake Facebook login page that looks identical to the real one. Victims enter their credentials which are then stolen.
threats.mitigation: Implement HSTS, certificate pinning, and educate users about phishing. Facebook can use Safe Browsing APIs to detect and block phishing domains.

threats.title: Brute Force Login (CWE-307)
threats.description: If Facebook does not limit login attempts, a threat actor can systematically brute force using a wordlist built from publicly available profile information (birthdate, family names, significant events).
threats.mitigation: Implement account lockout or CAPTCHA after N failed attempts. Use rate limiting on the authentication endpoint.

threats.title: SQL Injection on Login Page (CWE-89)
threats.description: If input is not sanitized on the login page, a threat actor can inject SQL commands (e.g., ' OR '1'='1) to bypass authentication.
threats.mitigation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements on all database-facing code. Apply allow-list input validation.

threats.title: MFA Interception (T1111)
threats.description: Threat actor can intercept SMS-based MFA codes by compromising the mobile operator (SIM swapping) to gain access to a victim's Facebook account.
threats.mitigation: Encourage use of authenticator app-based MFA instead of SMS. This risk is partially transferred to the mobile operator.

threats.title: Session Cookie Theft (T1539)
threats.description: Threat actor steals authenticated session cookies to gain access to a victim's Facebook account without needing credentials.
threats.mitigation: Use HttpOnly and Secure flags on all session cookies. Encrypt cookies in transit. Implement short session expiration.

threats.title: Insufficient Session Expiration (CWE-613)
threats.description: Facebook allows old/expired tokens to still be used for authentication, enabling threat actors to reuse stolen tokens.
threats.mitigation: Enforce strict session expiration. Invalidate tokens server-side on logout.

threats.title: Cookie Without HttpOnly Flag (CWE-1004)
threats.description: If HttpOnly flag is missing, client-side scripts (e.g., via XSS) can read and steal session cookies.
threats.mitigation: Set HttpOnly flag on all session cookies to prevent JavaScript access.

threats.title: Cookie Reliance Without Integrity Check (CWE-565)
threats.description: Application blindly trusts cookies without verifying their integrity, allowing threat actors to forge or tamper with cookie values to bypass authentication.
threats.mitigation: Sign cookies with HMAC. Validate cookie integrity on every request.

threats.title: Data Breach - Mass User Data Exfiltration
threats.description: Attacker bypasses security systems to extract large amounts of user data including emails, phone numbers, and profile information. Data can be used for phishing, fraud, or sold on the dark web.
threats.mitigation: Implement defense-in-depth: network segmentation, intrusion detection, encryption at rest, and strict access controls on database servers.

threats.title: Insufficiently Protected Credentials (CWE-522)
threats.description: If user credentials are stored without proper encryption (e.g., plaintext or weak hashing), threat actors who access the database can read them directly.
threats.mitigation: Hash passwords using bcrypt or Argon2 with a salt. Never store plaintext passwords.

threats.title: Stored XSS via Profile Bio (CWE-79)
threats.description: Threat actor injects malicious <script> tags through the profile bio. The script is stored in the database and executes every time another user visits the profile.
threats.mitigation: Apply output encoding when rendering user-generated content (convert < to <). Use Content Security Policy (CSP) headers.

threats.title: Stored XSS via Display Name in Notifications (CWE-79)
threats.description: Threat actor injects payloads through display names which are rendered in HTML notification templates.
threats.mitigation: Validate input with regex allow-list when data enters the system to reject HTML characters.

threats.title: Mass Account Creation for Cyberbullying
threats.description: Threat actor creates many throwaway accounts to cyberbully other users, then deletes the accounts to erase evidence.
threats.mitigation: Implement account activity logging with non-repudiation. Require phone/email verification for new accounts. Rate-limit account creation.

threats.title: CSRF - Forced Action (CWE-352)
threats.description: Threat actor sends a crafted link that, when clicked by an authenticated user, forces them to perform unintended actions (e.g., changing password, posting content).
threats.mitigation: Implement CSRF tokens on all state-changing requests. Use SameSite cookie attribute.

threats.title: Malicious File Upload via Messenger
threats.description: If Messenger does not restrict file types, a threat actor can send malicious files (e.g., .exe, .php shell) disguised as normal attachments to other users.
threats.mitigation: Validate file types using magic bytes (not just file extension). Sandbox/scan uploaded files with antivirus. Whitelist allowed file types.

threats.title: Phishing Link Distribution via Messenger
threats.description: Compromised accounts send phishing links to victims' friends and contacts through Messenger, spreading the attack laterally.
threats.mitigation: Implement URL scanning on shared links. Warn users when clicking external links. Detect spam/phishing patterns in message content.

threats.title: DDoS via Botnet
threats.description: Threat actor sets up a botnet by spreading trojans via messages/mail, then uses infected devices as zombie agents to flood Facebook's servers with traffic beyond their handling capacity.
threats.mitigation: Use a CDN and DDoS protection service (e.g., Cloudflare). Implement rate limiting and traffic anomaly detection.

threats.title: Resource Exhaustion via Unlimited Upload (CWE-770)
threats.description: If Facebook does not limit file upload size or frequency, a threat actor can repeatedly upload large files to overload the server storage and processing capacity.
threats.mitigation: Set upload size and rate limits per user. Implement server-side throttling.

threats.title: Social Engineering on Server Admin
threats.description: Threat actor sends phishing emails to Facebook employees/admins and convinces them to install malicious applications, gaining privileged access to internal systems.
threats.mitigation: Security awareness training for employees. Enforce least privilege principle. Use hardware security keys for admin access.

threats.title: SQL Injection on Search Feature (CWE-89)
threats.description: If the search feature does not sanitize input, a threat actor can inject SQL into the search query to manipulate or extract data from the database.
threats.mitigation: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements. Apply allow-list input validation for dynamic SQL elements like ORDER BY.
